analyst_view.overall: Early view: A game between 18th and 17th, 11 days away. Andorra's first games after the Tenerife tragedy will shape this one; goalkeeper Jesús Owono faces a ban of four to 12 games under the disciplinary code, per one report, while Efe Akman's one-match yellow-card ban should already be served at Almería. Leganés's Francisco Montero should likewise have served his ban against Burgos, and Luis Carrión needs results quickly.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Leganés have conceded eight goals in Carrión's three games (1-1, 4-3, 1-3), and Andorra are likely to have a stand-in goalkeeper with Owono suspended. Both sides sit near the drop zone and need wins, which tends to open games up late.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners and I stay there. Leganés's possession game (about two-thirds of the ball against Albacete) should give them more than the 3.8 the site has, but that is likely to come out of Andorra's 5.6 rather than add to the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards. Leganés have had several suspensions lately and the stakes are high at the bottom, but Andorra will be careful after a month under scrutiny, so I hold at about six until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots, with 17.5 for Andorra. I lean lower: that split looks lopsided against a Leganés side that keeps the ball and took 17 shots in its last game, and Andorra's attack may still be without Lautaro De León if his ban runs on. I expect a more even, lower total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target, with 6.4 for Andorra. I lean lower for the same reason: Andorra's home share looks too high for this matchup. Leganés's own accuracy has been poor (one goal from 17 shots against Albacete, plus Morata's missed penalty).
